readmeExcerpt:
Flint: A Visualization Language for the AI Era

[**Project site**](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/) · [**中文主页**](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/zh) · [**MCP server**](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp) · [**Gallery**](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/gallery) Flint lets AI agents **reliably create expressive, good-looking and interactive charts** from simple, human-editable specs. Good-looking charts usually take verbose low-level settings that tangle visual, style and interaction logic together; Flint moves that work into a compiler, so the spec stays short. Use it as an [MCP server](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp) with your agent, or as an [npm library](https://www.npmjs.com/package/flint-chart) in your app. Flint supports **52 chart types across 5 rendering backends** ([Vega-Lite](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/), [ECharts](https://echarts.apache.org/), [Chart.js](https://www.chartjs.org/), [Plotly](https://plotly.com/javascript/) and native Excel charts), with **14 preset themes** and **23 interaction presets**.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1cda0fa-3ea7-41af-b3fd-a127bc83d641

🔊 Click the speaker icon for sound  

## Updates - **November 15, 2026** — Flint 1.1 brings maps and layout: maps with customizable boundaries, globes, routes and labelled points, framed to their data; charts that fit their canvas on every backend; and annotations as captions beside what they name. ([release notes](https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/releases/tag/1.1)) - **October 19, 2026** — Flint 1.0 introduces [Flint Interactive](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions): interaction presets, semantic events, and an interaction API that connects charts to your app. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for every release. ## Quick start ### With your agent (MCP server) Paste this into your agent, such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. It adds the Flint MCP server and draws your first chart: ```text Help me set up Flint as an MCP server named "flint"! 1. Add it to my client config, using whichever option my client supports: - a local (stdio) server: npx -y flint-chart-mcp - the hosted server over HTTP: https://flint.data-formulator.ai/mcp 2. Verify the setup by listing the available Flint chart types. 3. Show me a fun first chart: how many moons each planet has, in a Flint theme you like. ``` Then ask for charts in your own words, such as *"compare today's change for the Magnificent Seven stocks in Economist style, and let me hover to read each one"*. The agent opens a live chart in the conversation, or returns a PNG, an SVG or a backend-native spec. To set it up by hand, see the [MCP server guide](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp).

### In your app (npm library) ```bash npm install flint-chart ``` ```tsx import type { ChartAssemblyInput } from 'flint-chart'; import { FlintChart } from 'flint-chart/react'; const spec: ChartAssemblyInput = { data: { values: [ { Month: '2026-01', Users: 1200 }, { Month: '2026-02', Users: 1800 }, ] }, semantic_types: { Month: 'YearMonth', Users: 'Quantity' }, chart_spec: { chartType: 'Line Chart', encodings: { x: 'Month', y: 'Users' } }, theme_spec: 'economist', interaction_spec: { interactions: [{ type: 'inspect-index' }] }, }; ``` `flint-chart` comes with every backend it draws with; React is an optional peer, needed only for ``. Without React, `mountChart` from `flint-chart/interactive` mounts the same chart in any page, and `assembleVegaLite`, `assembleECharts`, `assembleChartjs`, `assemblePlotly` and `assembleExcel` compile a spec into each library's own. To have your coding agent build it, point it at Flint's [chart](agent-skills/flint-chart-author/SKILL.md) and [interaction](agent-skills/flint-interaction-author/SKILL.md) authoring skills. ## How it works A Flint spec is the data, semantic types, a chart spec, and optional theme and interaction specs. Instead of leaving the glue to you, the compiler resolves each part against the others and composes a complete spec for the backend.

- **Describe data with semantic types.** Fields carry types such as `Rank`, `YearMonth`, `Delta` or `Temperature`, with their domains and units, and the compiler infers parsing, scales, axes, formatting and colors from them. - **Build charts with library-agnostic chart specs.** Charts name a chart type and its encodings; the compiler sizes, spaces and labels them for their data, and the same spec renders on every backend. See the [gallery](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/gallery). - **Unify the look with a theme spec.** Pick a preset such as the New York Times, the Economist or Swiss, or extend one with your brand: `{ extends: 'economist', id: 'our-brand', ink: { series: { single: '#6b3fa0' } } }`. See the [theme explorer](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/themes) and the [Theme Lab](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/theme-lab). - **Add interactions with an interaction spec.** Brushing, hover readouts, legend toggles and more; the compiler turns a reader's gestures into semantic events, so your app answers with high-level chart updates. See the [interaction gallery](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions/gallery) and [advanced interactions](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions/advanced). ## Documentation - [Project site](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/): gallery, live editor, themes and interactions - [API reference](docs/api-reference.md), with backend references for [Vega-Lite](docs/reference-vegalite.md), [ECharts](docs/reference-echarts.md), [Chart.js](docs/reference-chartjs.md), [Plotly](docs/reference-plotly.md) and [Excel](docs/reference-excel.md) - [Theme guide](docs/theme-spec.md), [interaction spec](docs/interaction-spec.md) and [interaction API](docs/interaction-api.md) - [MCP server guide](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp) and [agent skills](agent-skills/) - [Paper on arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20775) A Python port is in preview as source in [`packages/flint-py`](packages/flint-py); its package is not yet released. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome, especially new [chart templates](docs/adding-a-chart-template.md) and [rendering backends](docs/adding-a-backend.md). See [CONTRIBUTING](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md), and the [development guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) for setup, commands and the repository layout. Pick up an [issue](https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/issues), add a chart template or a theme, or share what you build. ## Community Join the [Flint Discord](https://discord.gg/hnm4Y8YX8) to ask questions, share your charts and follow releases.

readmeHtml:
Flint: A Visualization Language for the AI Era

Project site · 中文主页 · MCP server · Gallery

Flint lets AI agents reliably create expressive, good-looking and interactive charts from simple, human-editable specs. Good-looking charts usually take verbose low-level settings that tangle visual, style and interaction logic together; Flint moves that work into a compiler, so the spec stays short.

Use it as an MCP server with your agent, or as an npm library in your app. Flint supports 52 chart types across 5 rendering backends (Vega-Lite, ECharts, Chart.js, Plotly and native Excel charts), with 14 preset themes and 23 interaction presets.

flint-interactive-EN-white-web.mp4

🔊 Click the speaker icon for sound  

Updates

  • November 15, 2026 — Flint 1.1 brings maps and layout: maps with customizable boundaries, globes, routes and labelled points, framed to their data; charts that fit their canvas on every backend; and annotations as captions beside what they name. (release notes)
  • October 19, 2026 — Flint 1.0 introduces Flint Interactive: interaction presets, semantic events, and an interaction API that connects charts to your app.

See the changelog for every release.

Quick start

With your agent (MCP server)

Paste this into your agent, such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. It adds the Flint MCP server and draws your first chart:

Help me set up Flint as an MCP server named "flint"!

1. Add it to my client config, using whichever option my client supports:
   - a local (stdio) server: npx -y flint-chart-mcp
   - the hosted server over HTTP: https://flint.data-formulator.ai/mcp
2. Verify the setup by listing the available Flint chart types.
3. Show me a fun first chart: how many moons each planet has, in a Flint theme you like.

Then ask for charts in your own words, such as "compare today's change for the Magnificent Seven stocks in Economist style, and let me hover to read each one". The agent opens a live chart in the conversation, or returns a PNG, an SVG or a backend-native spec. To set it up by hand, see the MCP server guide.

In your app (npm library)

npm install flint-chart
import type { ChartAssemblyInput } from 'flint-chart';
import { FlintChart } from 'flint-chart/react';

const spec: ChartAssemblyInput = {
  data: { values: [
    { Month: '2026-01', Users: 1200 },
    { Month: '2026-02', Users: 1800 },
  ] },
  semantic_types: { Month: 'YearMonth', Users: 'Quantity' },
  chart_spec: { chartType: 'Line Chart', encodings: { x: 'Month', y: 'Users' } },
  theme_spec: 'economist',
  interaction_spec: { interactions: [{ type: 'inspect-index' }] },
};

<FlintChart spec={spec} />

flint-chart comes with every backend it draws with; React is an optional peer, needed only for <FlintChart>. Without React, mountChart from flint-chart/interactive mounts the same chart in any page, and assembleVegaLite, assembleECharts, assembleChartjs, assemblePlotly and assembleExcel compile a spec into each library's own. To have your coding agent build it, point it at Flint's chart and interaction authoring skills.

How it works

A Flint spec is the data, semantic types, a chart spec, and optional theme and interaction specs. Instead of leaving the glue to you, the compiler resolves each part against the others and composes a complete spec for the backend.

  • Describe data with semantic types. Fields carry types such as Rank, YearMonth, Delta or Temperature, with their domains and units, and the compiler infers parsing, scales, axes, formatting and colors from them.
  • Build charts with library-agnostic chart specs. Charts name a chart type and its encodings; the compiler sizes, spaces and labels them for their data, and the same spec renders on every backend. See the gallery.
  • Unify the look with a theme spec. Pick a preset such as the New York Times, the Economist or Swiss, or extend one with your brand: { extends: 'economist', id: 'our-brand', ink: { series: { single: '#6b3fa0' } } }. See the theme explorer and the Theme Lab.
  • Add interactions with an interaction spec. Brushing, hover readouts, legend toggles and more; the compiler turns a reader's gestures into semantic events, so your app answers with high-level chart updates. See the interaction gallery and advanced interactions.

Documentation

  • Project site: gallery, live editor, themes and interactions
  • API reference, with backend references for Vega-Lite, ECharts, Chart.js, Plotly and Excel
  • Theme guide, interaction spec and interaction API
  • MCP server guide and agent skills
  • Paper on arXiv

A Python port is in preview as source in packages/flint-py; its package is not yet released.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome, especially new chart templates and rendering backends. See CONTRIBUTING, and the development guide for setup, commands and the repository layout. Pick up an issue, add a chart template or a theme, or share what you build.

Community

Join the Flint Discord to ask questions, share your charts and follow releases.

releases.name: Flint 1.1: Maps and better layouts
releases.body: ### TLDR We have better maps now! and layouts are getting more robust!! :) ### Details ### Maps - **Boundaries:** maps draw customizable boundaries (`chartProperties.boundaries`): a named set, or a file of your own. - **Framing:** a map frames the country, region or continent its rows cover (`fit`), in a projection centred on it. - **Globes:** `projection: "orthographic"` turns to face the data and hides the far side; drag to turn it. - **Choropleth classes:** five quantile classes by default; `classes` takes `equal`, `jenks` or `continuous`. - **Map styles:** `mapStyle` names a ground (`atlas`, `dark`, `muted`, …) or restates its colours (`{ sea, land, coast, border }`). - **US counties:** `level: "auto"` draws states, then counties as you zoom in. - **Routes:** `order` joins points into routes, each leg bowed with an arrowhead whose tip sits on its stop; `strokeWidth` sets each leg's width. A route draws a dot at its start; every stop takes a dot where `size`, `shape`, `text` or a quantity's `color` asks for one, laid beneath the l

releases.name: Flint 1.0: Interactivity
releases.body: ## Flint 1.0: the language for interactive data visualizations In this release, Flint makes interactions easy to specify: from linked brushing and annotations to semantic zoom and coordinated chart–table views. Start with ready-made presets or build custom behaviors using data-level events and update operators. You describe the interaction; Flint handles the low-level wiring. Interaction support is now available in both the [MCP server](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp) and the [npm library](https://www.npmjs.com/package/flint-chart)! Explore the [interaction presets](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions/gallery), try the [custom interaction demos](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions/advanced), or dive into the [interaction API](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/documentation/interaction-api) to build your own. Watch the video below to learn more. :) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23b1fa91-ed7a-4c1f-8211-25c058d8aad6 ## Examples

## flint-chart 0.5.1

**Added**

- **Plotly theme support** — `theme_spec` now realizes onto Plotly figures.
- **Calendar Heatmap** chart type for Vega-Lite.

**Titles**

- Headlines *and* decks are fitted instead of widening the graphic, with or without a theme.
- Axis titles lie flat at the head of their own ruler; units are stated once.

**Grid and scales**

- Gridded axes round so the plot edge lands on a grid line, and the grid runs out to its number.
- A chart is never left with no way to read a value — where nothing is printed, the grid returns.

**Houses** — Economist type recalibrated; McKinsey's tick labels no longer outrank its subtitle.

**Security** — react-router CSRF and two other high-severity dev alerts resolved; production audit clean.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/compare/0.5...0.5.1
New contributor: @zl190

releases.name: Flint 0.5: ThemeSpec
releases.body:
Flint 0.5 introduces `ThemeSpec`, a formal specification for applying a coherent design system across an entire chart library. Instead of requiring creators or agents to reproduce design guidance chart by chart, a ThemeSpec participates directly in compilation and adapts to the chart's semantics, data, cardinality, and available space. A ThemeSpec shapes compilation in three stages. Using resolved semantic information, it: - governs layout constraints and dynamics, including density, spacing, sizing, and stretch limits; - conditionally resolves visual preferences for labels, legends, axes, annotations, and semantic roles; and - supplies design fixtures such as typography, color, surfaces, mark geometry, and structural line styles to backend-specific code generation.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A visualization intermediate language that lets AI agents create expressive charts from simple specs.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Flint is a visualization language designed specifically for the AI era. It acts as an intermediate layer, allowing AI agents to generate polished, expressive charts from human-readable specifications. It simplifies the process of creating complex data visualizations by bridging the gap between raw data and visual output. It provides a structured format that both LLMs and humans can understand and modify. This enables seamless integration of data visualization capabilities into various AI-driven applications and workflows.
keyFeatures: AI-native format: Designed to be easily generated and parsed by large language models.
Human-editable specs: Uses a simple specification format that developers can easily read and modify.
Polished visual output: Renders high-quality, expressive charts from the intermediate representation.
MCP Server support: Includes integration guides for Model Context Protocol servers.
Cross-platform design: Aims to be a universal intermediate language for data visualization tasks.
